analysis.title: Korea: From panic to FOMO
key_insights: Korean equities are surging as AI names rebound from major technical support, led by SK Hynix's results. Hedge funds had been cutting Korea exposure and buying downside protection during the washout, and are now being forced to chase the rebound.
KOSPI bounced off major support and remains below its 200-day moving average, which sits 7-8% higher. The note expects the market to spend time trading inside a wide range.
SK Hynix rose 11% on results: revenue of 104tr won (+328% YoY) vs 98tr won consensus, operating profit of 83.3tr won vs 76tr won expected. It plans up to $75bn in shareholder returns.
SK Hynix has long-term deals with 14 major customers that secure over 50% of 2027-28 capacity, and the company expects memory demand to exceed supply through 2030.
SK Hynix bounced off its long-term trendline and is back at its 200-day moving average. Samsung also bounced off its long-term trendline and has already reclaimed its 200-day moving average.
Hedge funds have been the standout net sellers of Korea and Taiwan in Asia, so the rebound is running into a market where investors recently cut risk.
Goldman data shows net allocation to Korea fell to 3.4% (29th percentile over one year, 86th over five years) and gross allocation fell to 2.4% (30th percentile over one year, 86th over five years).

KOSPI's spot-up, vol-up regime has faded. Volatility was bid during the early October selloff but has not followed the latest rally. Traders paid up for downside protection during the washout and are now being forced to chase upside.

JPM's October 20 note said Korean equities trade at record-low forward P/E multiples. Excluding the memory giants, KOSPI trades at 8.4x forward earnings, the 11th percentile historically, and RSI fell to its lowest since Liberation Day with extreme numbers of oversold stocks.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix rose 11% after revenue of 104tr won (+328% YoY) beat the 98tr won consensus and operating profit of 83.3tr won beat the 76tr won expected. The company plans up to $75bn in shareholder returns.
Samsung surged overnight after bouncing off its long-term trendline and has already reclaimed its 200-day moving average.

SK Hynix plans up to $75bn in shareholder returns. It has long-term deals with 14 major customers securing over 50% of 2027-28 capacity.
risk_factors: KOSPI remains below its 200-day moving average, 7-8% higher, and the note expects a wide trading range.
Positioning is light after hedge fund selling, so the rebound could be a violent move inside a range rather than the start of a larger trend.

tension_points.bull_case: SK Hynix's results beat consensus and demand is expected to exceed supply through 2030. Valuations are at record lows, and underweight positioning means investors must chase the rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: KOSPI is still below its 200-day moving average, which is 7-8% higher, and the market probably needs to trade inside a wide range. The rally may be just another violent move inside that range.
